name: Works Contract Review
items: Each value, percentage or period is stated once; other clauses refer to it instead of repeating it
The same item (period, percentage, penalty) is not given different values in different clauses, and amounts in words match figures
Recitals and introductions only refer to the operative clause and do not restate price, warranty, periods or scope
The pricing basis is consistent across the recitals, the Contract Value, payment and variation clauses
Cross-references point to an existing clause and name its section (Form of Agreement, General Conditions, Special Conditions)
No leftovers from other projects, wrong entity names, or tender-stage content (Instructions to Tenderers, bid validity, submission instructions)
The Contract Documents are listed in order of priority, and every listed document (specifications, drawings, BOQ, maintenance volume) exists
Every capitalized term is defined once and used consistently; no undefined variants
No 'etc.' in obligations, and no slash roles such as 'Employer/Engineer'
Variations can be instructed without the Contractor's consent; disputed value or time is determined by the Engineer while work continues
Rates for extra items without a BOQ rate are determined by the Engineer if not agreed, without delaying the Works
Extension-of-time claims have a notice time bar (for example 28 days) and require an effect on the critical path
Employer delays (late approvals, late drawings) do not add time automatically; late site handover gives time only, not cost
Delay damages (liquidated damages) have a rate, a cap, and apply without prejudice to other remedies; no clause caps all delay costs at that amount
Termination for convenience pays only for work executed and materials delivered, with no loss of profit
The Contractor has no right to suspend work for a reasonable payment delay; late compensation claims are waived after a stated period
The Contractor's liability is not capped, and indemnities survive termination
Advance payment, performance bond and retention: amounts, validity, reduction and release conditions are stated and consistent
Bank guarantee forms are unconditional, irrevocable and payable on first written demand
Preliminary acceptance, final acceptance and the warranty (defects liability) period are defined, with start dates and outstanding-work obligations
Design responsibility is clear: what the Employer provides and what the Contractor must review, coordinate and redesign at no extra cost
Key personnel are listed with qualifications, stay full-time until preliminary acceptance, and are replaced only with approval
Sub-contractor approval does not relieve the Contractor of responsibility and liability
Insurance, force majeure (special risks) notice periods, and termination after prolonged special risks are stated
Dispute resolution, governing law, jurisdiction and contract language are stated
Scope of work is short in the agreement and refers to the Contract Documents; everything the Contractor must deliver is inside the Contract

name: Research Paper Check
items: The research question or aim is stated clearly near the start
Every claim of fact is supported by a citation or by the paper's own results
The method is described in enough detail to repeat it (materials, quantities, conditions, instruments)
Units, symbols and significant figures are consistent across text, tables and figures
Every table and figure is referred to in the text and has a clear caption
Results and discussion are kept apart, and conclusions do not go beyond the results
Limitations of the study are stated
References are complete and in one consistent style
